title: splunk-otel-db2 values
description: Helm validates these before any template renders, so a wrong type is reported as a values error rather than surfacing later as a template failure or, worse, rendering something that looks valid. Template-level checks are kept only for rules a schema cannot express, such as requiring a port when TLS is on.

enabled.description: Read by a parent chart's `condition: <alias>.enabled`, not by this chart's templates. Present so the subchart stays disabled when a parent's own key is absent, as under `helm upgrade --reuse-values` from a release predating it. Ignored by a standalone install.

items.description: Closed to extra keys: the chart reads exactly the properties below, so an unrecognised one is a typo. Left open, `collectionIntervl` validated cleanly and the receiver silently ran on the default instead.

name.description: Lowercase DNS-compatible. Uppercased into env-var keys, so hyphens and underscores would collide.

port.description: Typed as an integer so null or a string is rejected here. Db2 requires ssl_svcename to differ from svcename, so with TLS on this must be the TLS listener's port.

collectionInterval.description: Whole seconds, minutes or hours, as in '30s', '5m' or '1h'. Mirrors what the receiver's parser accepts: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and leading zeros are allowed, but an all-zero value is not. Matched here so '500ms' or '0s' is a values error rather than a receiver that exits at startup.

serviceInstanceId.description: Overrides the service.instance.id resource attribute. Empty means unset, as elsewhere in this file, and the receiver composes one from hostname, port and database. Anything else must begin and end with a non-whitespace character: the receiver treats a blank override as absent and uses an untrimmed value verbatim, so ' ' would be silently discarded and ' id ' would become an identity with spaces in it. Both are rejected here instead.

tls.description: Typed so `tls: true` is rejected. null is allowed and means "take the defaults", which the template normalises - rejecting a bare `tls:` would be unhelpful for something harmless.

insecure.description: Boolean, so the string "false" is rejected rather than being read as truthy and silently disabling the TLS-port check.

insecureSkipVerify.description: Skip checking the certificate was issued for the configured hostname. Named and sensed to match exporters.otlp.tls and the collector's database receivers, which default it to true; here it is false.

caSecret.description: Name of an existing Secret holding a certificate authority to trust. Matched as a true DNS subdomain — dot-separated labels, each 1–63 characters and starting and ending alphanumeric — so names the Kubernetes API would reject, such as `a..b` or `a.-b`, are caught here rather than surfacing later as a Secret reference that cannot be resolved.

caSecretKey.description: Key within caSecret holding the PEM certificate. Constrained to the characters Kubernetes allows in a Secret key: the volume projects this key by name, and a key that cannot exist would leave the pod unable to mount.
